title: Multi model multimodal and multi agent innovations in Azure AI: Cedric Vidal

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk is a demo-driven showcase of Azure AI Studio as a developer platform—model catalog, deployment options, evaluation tools, code interpreter, and GitHub Workspaces—rather than a single end-user application. Azure AI is a platform that software builders use to construct AI systems across multiple verticals. Demos cover model selection with benchmarks, serverless vs. bring-your-own deployment, and quality evaluation using coherence, groundedness, and relevance metrics. Assumes familiarity with Azure AI Studio, multimodal AI, and RAG concepts but remains demo-focused with introductory technical depth. Recorded conference presentation with live demos at the AI Engineer World's Fair. Multiple direct transcript evidence anchors with exact quotes and character offsets support the platform classification.

summary: Cedric Vidal introduces a demo-focused session on Azure AI's multi-model, multimodal, multilingual, and multi-agent capabilities. He positions Azure AI as a comprehensive platform partnering with OpenAI while offering many additional models for text, vision, and speech, all under a responsible AI framework. Build announcements include GA of AI Studio, GPT-4o, Phi-3 from Microsoft Research, GPT-4 Turbo Vision, DALL-E 3, Whisper, the Assistant API for building agents, a new batch inference API, and a video translation service. The first set of demos uses GPT-4o Vision on restaurant menus—one printed and one handwritten in French—showing the model's ability to extract text, reason about vegan options, and translate simultaneously, demonstrating native multimodal understanding versus traditional OCR pipelines. Vidal then shows infrastructure monitoring use cases: fallen electric poles for the energy industry and a damaged house for insurance, noting that JSON output can enable automated dashboards. He demonstrates Azure's video translation service, which translates speech into other languages while preserving the speaker's own voice and intonation. He showcases the Azure AI model catalog with 1,600 models, two deployment options (serverless pay-per-token and bring-your-own infrastructure), and model benchmarks for selecting appropriate models. He demos Phi-3 Vision on the same electric pole scenario and shows Phi-3 3.8B running locally in the browser using WebGPU, noting its speed on a MacBook Pro M2 and its ability to process sensitive data offline. Vidal then demonstrates RAG by grounding a model in Wikipedia pages about Rivian models, showing how it provides up-to-date information beyond the model's training cutoff, though a live demo bug required switching models. He shows Azure AI Studio's evaluation feature for measuring coherence, groundedness, and relevance of LLM applications. Next, he demonstrates a code interpreter agent by uploading a GPX file from a kite surfing session, asking questions about duration, number of tacks, and visualizing the route on a map—the LLM automatically generates and executes Python code in a sandbox. Finally, he previews GitHub Workspaces, showing an LLM analyzing a Python repository and generating a Java GUI frontend, with capabilities for specifications, planning, and corrections.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

GPT-4o Vision natively understands pixels and text together, enabling combined OCR-level extraction plus reasoning and translation in a single model call

Azure's video translation service preserves the speaker's original voice and intonation across languages

sections.title: Introduction and Session Overview
sections.summary: Cedric Vidal introduces himself as Principal AI Advocate at Microsoft and outlines the session focus on multi-model, multimodal, multilingual, and multi-agent AI, noting the session is almost entirely demos.

sections.title: Build Announcements
sections.summary: Recap of Build announcements: GA of AI Studio, GPT-4o with text/vision/speech, Phi-3 from MS Research, GPT-4 Turbo Vision, DALL-E 3, Whisper, Assistant API, batch inference API, and video translation service.

sections.title: GPT-4o Vision: Restaurant Menu Demos
sections.summary: Demos of GPT-4o Vision on a printed restaurant menu (identifying vegan options by mixing text extraction with reasoning) and a handwritten French chalkboard menu (recognizing handwriting, translating French to English, and reasoning simultaneously). Emphasizes native multimodal understanding versus traditional OCR pipelines.

sections.title: GPT-4o Vision: Infrastructure and Insurance Use Cases
sections.summary: Demos showing GPT-4o Vision analyzing fallen electric poles for energy industry infrastructure monitoring and a damaged tilted house for insurance assessment. Notes the ability to request JSON output for automated dashboards and real-time monitoring.

sections.title: Azure AI Video Translation Service
sections.summary: Demo of Azure's video translation service that translates speech into other languages in the speaker's own voice while preserving intonation (whispering and yelling patterns maintained).

sections.title: Model Catalog, Deployment Options, and Benchmarks
sections.summary: Overview of the Azure AI model catalog with 1,600 models, two deployment options (serverless pay-per-token and bring-your-own infrastructure), and model benchmarks for comparing accuracy and metrics to select appropriate models.

sections.title: Phi-3 Vision and Local Browser Inference
sections.summary: Demo of Phi-3 Vision (Microsoft Research's smaller multimodal model) on the same electric pole use case, showing good results despite smaller size. Then shows Phi-3 3.8B (4-bit quantized, ~2GB) downloading and running locally in the browser using WebGPU.

sections.title: Phi-3 Local Inference Performance and Offline Capability
sections.summary: Continues the Phi-3 local browser demo, noting fast inference on a MacBook Pro M2 with Apple Silicon GPU support. Highlights that the model runs locally so Wi-Fi can be disconnected, making it interesting for processing sensitive data.

sections.title: RAG Demo with Rivian Models
sections.summary: Demonstrates RAG by grounding a model in uploaded Wikipedia pages about Rivian models. Shows that GPT-4 Turbo (last updated April 2023) only knows R1T, R1S, and Rivian truck, while RAG-enabled queries return the R3 and R2. A live demo bug with one model required switching to 3.5 Turbo.

sections.title: Azure AI Studio Model Evaluation
sections.summary: Shows the evaluation feature in AI Studio for measuring LLM application quality using coherence, groundedness, and relevance metrics. Groundedness is especially important for RAG applications to ensure answers are grounded in documents. Scores range from 1 to 5.

sections.title: Code Interpreter Agent: Kite Surfing GPX Analysis
sections.summary: Demonstrates an agent with code interpreter by uploading a GPX file from a kite surfing session. The LLM automatically generates and executes Python code in a sandbox to answer questions about duration (42 minutes), number of tacks (117), draw the session on a map, and add red crosses for turns—all without the user knowing the GPX file format.

sections.title: GitHub Workspaces Preview
sections.summary: Previews GitHub Workspaces, where an LLM analyzes a Python repository and generates a Java GUI frontend. The system writes specifications, generates plans, and allows corrections at each step. Noted as preview, not yet generally available.
